paragraphs.text: Run coding agents on any SSH host as if it were local: one persistent connection, native file editin
g, search, exec, terminals and port forwards, with nothing installed remotely.
# Presence
**Your SSH hosts, as local tabs.**

Persistent remote workspaces, native file editing, search, exec, terminals and port
forwards for cod
ing agents — with **nothing installed on the remote host**.
English · 简体中文 · Releases · MCP server

> ⚠️ **A local session is not bound to a remote workspace.** Opening a remote workspace in
> Presenc

e does not turn a local agent session into a remote one. When your session's
> working directory is

outside the presence mounts root, `presence_exec` and every other
> `presence_*` tool require an exp

licit `host` (or `PRESENCE_HOST`); without one they refuse
> with the session's cwd instead of silen

tly running on the last-activated machine. Sessions
> started inside a remote workspace resolve to t

hat machine automatically. See
> Known limits.
## Why

Running an agent on every remote machine means installing it N times, upgrading it N
times and confi

guring proxies per host. Running `ssh host '<command>'` from the local
agent means a new handshake p
er command, no native file tools and no continuity.

Presence keeps the agent local and **extends its reach through one persistent SSH
connection per hos
t**. The remote side is still plain `sshd`: SFTP, exec and a PTY.
| Approach | Cost |

| Install the agent on every host | N installs, N upgrades, per-host proxying |
| `ssh host '<comman

d>'` per call | Handshake per command, no file tools, no sessions |
| **Presence** | One connection
per host, native tools, nothing installed remotely |
## Features
- **Remote zero-install** — uses only `sshd` built-ins: the SFTP subsystem, exec channels and a PTY.

- **One handshake** — a pool keeps one connection per host; every later call is a request on it.
-
**Native remote tools** — `rg`/`grep` runs on the target, commands run in the target shell; path, pe

rmission and encoding semantics are the remote ones.
- **Local-like edits** — atomic writes, mode pr

eservation, ambiguity refusal, read-before-write guard, `presence_edit` with dry-run diffs.
- **Real
workspaces** — a remote directory becomes a normal DSH workspace with a file tree and terminals tha

t open **on the remote machine**.
- **Sessions are scoped (0.20 hotfix)** — a local session no longe
r silently borrows the last-activated remote workspace: `presence_*` needs an explicit `host` or `PR

ESENCE_HOST`, and the system prompt tells each session whether it is local or remote.
- **Conditions
instead of sleeps** — `presence_wait` blocks on a file (`exists`/`minBytes`/`mtimeAfter`), a grep m
atch count, a process (`pid`/`pattern`), a port state or a job id; a timeout is `met:false`, not an

error.
- **Jobs that survive a restart** — background jobs are persisted to `~/.dsh/presence/jobs.js
on` with pid/pgid. `logPath` is the job log to tail; `commandLogPath` is the command's own log and e
quals `logPath` on current kernels (a separate wrapper log only exists when a kernel records one) —
use `commandLogPath ?? logPath`. After a restart their state is `unknown` until probed — never a fal

se `running`, and an exit code may be missing.
- **Batch transfer and append** — `presence_import`/`
presence_export` take `paths[]` (1–50) or a glob and return per-file results; `presence_write { mode

:"append" }` appends without rewriting the file.
- **Recoverable deletes** — destructive shell comma

nds dry-run first; `presence_trash` moves paths to a remote trash with restore.
- **`@` completes re
mote files** — inside a remote workspace, file-reference completion indexes the machine itself (`rg

--files`, `find` fallback), not a local mirror.
[该节后续省略]

### A real trajectory

These three figures are rendered from a recorded 22-call session: train an MNIST
classifier twice on

a remote 64-core host, compare two learning rates, and export
the result. Every row is one tool cal

l with its measured duration; red rows are
real failures kept verbatim.

Figure 3 stacks end-to-end time into think / wait / tool. The same task through
bare ssh/scp takes 4

52.5 s versus 272.8 s, with a 10.4×
higher median interaction latency.
## Quick start
### 1. Install the DSH plugin
[代码示例省略，未执行]
From a source checkout:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
### 2. Pick a host and open a workspace

Open **Settings → Presence → New**, choose a host from `~/.ssh/config` (or paste a
manual `ssh` comm

and), then pick a remote folder. It appears as a workspace; the
left sidebar, file tree, terminal an
d agent tools all use that remote directory.

A session started in that workspace is remote. A session started anywhere else (for
example a normal

local project) stays local: it must pass `host` explicitly — or set
`PRESENCE_HOST` — before callin
g `presence_exec` / `presence_*`.
## How it works
[代码示例省略，未执行]
| Agent operation | Channel | Remote dependency |

| read / write / edit / list / stat | SFTP subsystem | `sftp-server` (stock sshd) |
| exec, search (

`rg`/`grep`), git | exec channel | commands already on the host |
| interactive terminal | shell cha
nnel + PTY | the host's login shell |
Measured on a Linux host:
| Operation | Latency |

| `ssh host '<cmd>'` (new connection every time) | 520–540 ms |
| Presence connect (one handshake, k

ey auth) | 145 ms |
| Presence `sftp stat` | p50 0.6 ms / p95 0.9 ms |
| Presence `exec true` (new c

hannel + shell) | p50 7.6 ms |
| 8 concurrent exec channels | 15 ms total |

> Keep TCP_NODELAY on: without it, request/response hits delayed ACK and p95 goes
> from 0.9 ms to 4

p TCP_NODELAY on: without it, request/response hits delayed ACK and p95 goes
> from 0.9 ms to 48 ms.
